Sensitive accesses and system calls observed while the app was in the background or the screen was off. Call outcomes are unavailable. This includes apps running under a system identity. Refusals, always-on system processes and low-level services are excluded.

Conversations in which the app sent at least 4 KB while in the background, that is, not on screen: running behind a notification or always on, switched away from, or with the screen off. Only the bytes measured are told; nothing is guessed about what was sent or why.

One app reading one kind of data many times within any 60 minutes, counting only reads that went through, plus system calls, whose outcome can\'t be seen. The limit is 10 for the clipboard and device identifiers, 20 for contacts, messages, call history, calendar, accounts and the app list, and 60 for everything else.

Jiumi log export
Range: %1$s
Exported: %2$s

Files
timeline.csv: one row per record, as the in-app timeline shows it with merged records opened. For reading and analysis.
sessions.csv: each monitoring session with its start, end, monitored time, interruptions and lost records.
raw/accesses.csv: permission accesses reported live by AppOps, as recorded.
raw/calls.csv: system service and database (content provider) calls seen by call tracing, as recorded.
raw/connections.csv: network connections; byte counts need platform support and are empty without it.
raw/dns.csv: with Record domains on, the domains each app looked up and the addresses they resolved to; result is the DNS result code (0 found, 3 no such name, -1 no answer).
raw/process_starts.csv: process starts while monitoring.
raw/monitor_events.csv: monitor starts, heartbeats and stops, from which monitored time is worked out.
diagnostics/pairing.log: the Wireless debugging pairing log, for troubleshooting.

Fields
Times are local with their offset; time_ms is milliseconds since the epoch.
app_state: top foreground, fgsvc foreground service, fg visible, bg background, cch cached, gone not running, pers persistent system process.
refused: Android refused the access.
result (raw/accesses.csv): 0 allowed, 1 ignored, 2 errored, 3 decided by the permission, 4 foreground only.
same_action_calls: system calls counted as the same action, with their counts.
routine_system_work: routine work of system services and hardware daemons.

The permission usage record\'s count of this app\'s access, including time before monitoring began and parts of the system Jiumi can\'t watch live. It has only how often, not when; background means not in use, as elsewhere in Jiumi. Older counts are kept in longer stretches, so a range\'s edges are approximate.

Android\'s alarm service counts these since the phone last started: each time one of this app\'s alarms woke the phone from sleep to run it. Alarms that went off while the phone was already awake aren\'t counted.

You can uninstall apps that came with the phone for the current user only. The factory copy and app data stay on the phone. You can usually restore the app under Apps › Uninstalled. Uninstalling some apps may affect phone features, and you assume that risk.
Opens up most core system components, apps the phone relies on, default apps, and access changes that reach past one app. A change may stop the phone from starting; the risk is yours.
While open, Jiumi checks apps it disabled every few minutes. It records detected re-enables in the timeline.

You can then disable or uninstall components bound deeply into the system, apps the phone relies on and default apps, and change access that also affects other apps, users or firewall rules. This can break related features, or at worst stop the phone from starting, leaving only a factory reset, which erases what is on it.

Jiumi, essential system components, persistent system apps and the active keyboard are protected against disabling and uninstalling.

Jiumi sets up a VPN on this phone that receives DNS queries only, and records which domains each app looks up; connections then show the domain, not just the IP. Queries go unchanged to the DNS servers of the network you are on, other traffic never passes through Jiumi, and nothing leaves the phone. Another VPN can\'t run at the same time.

Private DNS is set to a named provider, so lookups go straight to it and no domains can be recorded. Set it to Automatic or Off in the system settings.

Another app\'s VPN is on. Android runs one VPN at a time, so no domains can be recorded while it is. If it is a proxy, apps\' connections also show the addresses it hands out (often 198.18.x.x) instead of where they really go. Turn it off for a full record.
The VPN isn\'t running; another VPN may have replaced it. Turn this off and on again to restore it.
